structure: Use one stochastic, positively dependent rank law anchored to the reported within-sex Pearson correlation. Incorporate feasibility into assignment rather than relying on host projection. Assignment takes O(N log N) time and O(N) memory. Do not add an unsupported disease-mixture parameter or fit the regression and correlation as independent evidence.
parameter_provenance: The female and male Pearson anchors of 0.96 come directly from Table 2 for the same participants as the supplied marginal moments.
Sex-specific arithmetic means and SDs from Table 1 determine the approximate lognormal-to-Gaussian correlation conversion; they do not replace the supplied marginal arrays.
Gaussian dependence, independent latent noise, and the feasible priority assignment are modeling choices, not findings reported by the source.
The rounded regression coefficients are supporting descriptions of the same dependence, not individual identities or additional calibration targets.
Equal female and male weights come from the task; source sample sizes are not used as population weights.
requested_estimands: Mean individual ratio: calculate the within-sex mean of FEV1/FVC on the generated pairs, then average the two sex-specific means with weights 0.5 and 0.5.
Ratio of population means: divide the equally sex-weighted FEV1 mean by the equally sex-weighted FVC mean. This quantity is fixed by the supplied columns and is unaffected by pairing.
Fraction strictly below 0.70: calculate mean(FEV1/FVC < 0.70) within each sex, then average with equal sex weights.

Within-sex volume correlation: calculate Pearson correlation separately for F and M on the generated pairs. If a single equal-sex summary is required, average these two correlations rather than using a pooled-sex correlation. Correlation is undefined for a constant or singleton margin.
limitations: Healthy never-smokers are not representative of a broader population including smokers or respiratory illness. Transporting their dependence is an explicit working assumption.
The source age range is 18–85, whereas the requested range is 18–79. Individual age and stature are unavailable, so neither age restriction nor covariate adjustment can be reproduced.
No bronchodilator intervention is described, supporting use as a pre-bronchodilator proxy but not establishing a documented pre-bronchodilator protocol.
Marginal moments and Pearson correlation do not identify the ratio distribution or its lower tail. The fraction below 0.70 is especially dependent on the chosen law.
Finite grids, random ranks, and feasibility assignment can move the achieved Pearson correlation away from 0.96. It is an anchor, not an exact output constraint.
If the sorted margins themselves fail FEV1 <= FVC elementwise, no feasible permutation exists; the generator raises an error rather than modifying either column.
Seed variation measures simulation variability under this law, not uncertainty about transportability or the dependence family.
checks_actually_performed: Analytical feasibility check: sorted elementwise FEV1 <= FVC is necessary and sufficient for a feasible permutation.
Analytical assignment check: at FVC index j, sorted feasibility guarantees at least j+1 eligible FEV1 values, of which only j have already been assigned; therefore the priority queue cannot be empty.
The executable includes runtime validation of inputs, permutation completeness, and every resulting volume inequality. These runtime checks have not been executed here.
No numerical simulation, achieved-correlation assessment, or target validation was performed; no target observations or execution tools were supplied.
